items.title: Eminem’s Publisher Eight Mile Style Sues Suno Over Allegations of Copyright Infringement
items.summary: Eminem’s publishing company, Eight Mile Style, has now filed litigation against Suno for allegedly reproducing their copyrighted works without permission or compensation. items.title: Elvis Presley Enterprises Slaps Suno With Copyright & NIL Suit, Says the Platform Was ‘Always Meant to Replace the Artists Whose Works and Identities Were Being Unlawfully Copied’
items.summary: Another day, another AI infringement lawsuit – this time against Suno, which is accused of infringing a number of Elvis Presley copyrights as well as the King of Rock’s name, image, and likeness (NIL) rights. Plaintiffs including Elvis Presley Enterprises, Raleigh Music Publishing, and a subsidiary of Elvis IP owner Au…

items.title: Reservoir Expands Its Suno and Anthropic Infringement Lawsuits; Publisher Now Seeks Nearly $450 Million in Statutory Damages
items.summary: Reservoir Media has supersized its Suno and Anthropic copyright infringement complaints, which are now demanding a combined total of nearly $450 million in statutory damages. New York City-headquartered Reservoir fired off the expanded actions yesterday, weeks after submitting the original complaints. As we broke down…

items.title: Tencent Music says AI content streams are ‘negligible’ – as it takes legal action over AI infringement
items.summary: TME says streams of AI-generated content are declining as a share of listening Source

items.title: Australia’s creative industries join forces to launch campaign against copyright reforms that favour big tech and AI companies
items.summary: With mounting concerns that the Australian government is considering copyright reforms to make it easier for AI companies to copy existing content without getting permission first, the country’s music community has joined the wider creative industries to launch a new campaign opposing those reforms

items.title: Australia’s ‘Not AI’s to Take’ campaign defends human creativity
items.summary: The Australian music industry has been fighting hard to persuade the country’s government not to throw copyright protection under the bus in order to attract big AI companies’ investment. The latest initiative is a campaign called ‘Not AI’s to Take’ which launched today. The post is from Music Ally .

items.title: Suno adds ‘Visuals’ tool for making lyric videos and album art
items.summary: In a way, it’s surprising that it took this long for Suno to expand into AI-generated video. Its new ‘Visuals’ tool can be used to create lyric videos, album art and other clips to accompany songs made on its platform. The post is from Music Ally .

items.title: Suno launches AI music video tool built on model from MiniMax – the Chinese AI firm being sued by Disney and other Hollywood studios
items.summary: 'Visuals' generates videos and images to accompany songs made on Suno's platform Source

items.title: Vast majority of consumers want AI music labelled, Deezer survey reveals, as SoundCloud and Spotify update AI policies and tools
items.summary: Deezer has surveyed 9000 consumers in nine markets about their attitudes towards AI music, with 80% of respondents saying AI tracks should be clearly labelled. The new stats coincide with updates from SoundCloud on its AI policies and Spotify on the roll out of its Artist Profile Protection feature

items.title: SoundCloud cracks down on AI slop as Spotify expands Artist Profile Protection
items.summary: Calls from the music industry for streaming services to do more to tackle AI slop, musical spam and streaming fraud are being answered – today by the latest moves from SoundCloud and Spotify. The post is from Music Ally .

tip.title: Registra antes de publicar, no después
tip.body: El registro de tu obra no crea el derecho de autor —ese nace con la creación— pero sí te da la prueba con fecha cierta que vale en un juicio. Regístrala antes de subirla a plataformas, no cuando ya tengas el problema.

tip.title: Register before you release, not after
tip.body: Registration doesn't create your copyright —that exists from the moment of creation— but it gives you dated proof that holds up in court. Register before uploading to platforms, not after trouble shows up.
